title: The normalized regular coefficient scalar unit is a quasi-isomorphism
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and any scheme $Y$. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $A_{F,m}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m$, $R_F=\varprojlim_{m\ge1}(A_{F,m})_Y$, and write $\pi^F_m:R_F\to(A_{F,m})_Y$ for the limit projections, for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the coefficient maps $\rho_m:R_E\to(A_{L,m})_Y$ induced by $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ as in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Let $P=R_E[0]$, and let $T_m=\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P\otimes_{R_E}(A_{L,m})_Y)$ with transition $t_m:T_{m+1}\to T_m$ induced by reduction. Tensors are sheafified tensors applied termwise [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; restriction uses $\pi^L_m$. Put $B=\prod_{m\ge1}T_m$ (termwise product) and $C_{E,L}=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:B\to B)[-1]$, where $(1-s)(x)_m=x_m-t_m(x_{m+1})$, with the strict mapping-cocone convention and projections $\mathrm{fst}:C_{E,L}\to B$, $\mathrm{snd}:C_{E,L}\to B[-1]$ on graded objects. All complexes and derived categories are those of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $\eta_{E,L}:R_L[0]\to C_{E,L}$ be the uniquely normalized chain map of [lem-weil-constant-scalar-strict-unit], with $m$-th product coordinate $s\mapsto1\otimes\pi^L_m(s)$ and zero shifted-product component. Each $A_{L,m}$ is finite; the transition maps of constant sheaves $(A_{L,m+1})_Y\to(A_{L,m})_Y$ are epimorphisms. The multiplication identifications $u_m:T_m\cong\operatorname{Res}^L_m(A_{L,m})_Y[0]$ identify their ordinary limit, with its projections, with $R_L[0]$. The map $\eta_{E,L}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. More precisely, the termwise product $B$ represents the product of the $T_m$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$, and for some $\delta$ the triangle
$$R_L[0]\xrightarrow{(u_m^{-1}\pi^L_m)_m}B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\xrightarrow{\delta}R_L[1]$$
is distinguished, hence a Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]. Under $u_m$, the inverse of $Q(\eta_{E,L})$ identifies the strict cone computing integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] with $R_L[0]$, compatibly with all the quotient projections; here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. For $E=L$ this is a distinguished Roos triangle whose first map is the prescribed reduction-unit map of $R_E[0]$, so $R_E[0]$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete]. These conclusions hold also for $E=L$, ramified extensions, disconnected $Y$, and $Y=\varnothing$, with no finiteness hypothesis on $Y$.

proof.text: The constant ring-presheaf map induced by the quotient factor map is sectionwise surjective. Mathlib Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_presheafToSheaf_map_iff carries this to the constant ring sheaves. Under the multiplication identifications, the underlying additive-sheaf maps of the tower transitions are these coefficient reductions. Transport local preimages through the degree-zero isomorphisms; local surjectivity implies epimorphy of additive sheaves, and faithful forgetting reflects epimorphy in modules.

Use the finite multiplication isomorphisms and inverse tensor formula of [lem-weil-constant-scalar-strict-unit]. The normalized legs have coefficient coordinate exactly pi_n, and the transition formula proves their compatibility. All nonzero degrees vanish. In degree zero, evaluate sheaves of modules at each site object and forget to sets. The termwise multiplication isomorphisms identify this cone with the limit cone defining the completed coefficient ring [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Mathlib reflection of limits through module forgetting, evaluation, and the fully faithful sheaf inclusion gives the ordinary limit with these exact legs.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59; explicit regular-module multiplication and limit-coordinate calculation

proof.text: Apply clause 1 of [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit] with $\mathcal R=R_L$ and the module sheaves $F_m$ of Step 3. Its hypotheses are exactly the arbitrary scheme $Y$, the sheaf of commutative rings $R_L$, and the epimorphic transitions established in Step 2. It gives an epimorphism $1-s$ on $\prod_m F_m$ with kernel the ordinary limit via its prescribed projections. Through the strict tower isomorphisms $u_m$, this says that $f=1-s:B\to B$ is degreewise epimorphic, and its kernel complex is $R_L[0]$ with inclusion $i=(u_m^{-1}\pi^L_m)_m$. Outside degree zero both source and target of $f$ are zero, so the degreewise epimorphism condition there is automatic.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.10, p. 17; Proposition 3.2.3(1), p. 18; Proposition 4.2.8, p. 29

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] to the degreewise epimorphic boundary. The ordinary limit is its kernel, by the product projection equations. Its unique isomorphism to the chosen kernel, followed by the kernel-to-shifted-cone quasi-isomorphism, has the same first and second graded projections as eta: the first is the specified kernel inclusion and the second is zero. Extensionality for the two mapping-cone summands, with the explicit shift-sign formulas, identifies this map with eta. Thus the specified eta is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Cone and shift convention, Tag 014Q; the cited kernel-to-cocone lemma supplies the chain comparison, with the strict normalization checked explicitly

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] to obtain CountableAB4Star for the actual completed module category. The proved general theorem [lem-weil-derived-countable-products-core] identifies Q of the termwise product with the product of the Q of its terms, with the actual product projections. Localize the mapping-cocone triangle and transport its first object through Q(eta); its first map is Q(inclusion) and its second map is Q(boundary). This gives the stated distinguished triangle and inverse-projection identities.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.10 and its proof, p. 17; Stacks derived.tex Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit), with 1-s convention

proof.text: Localization inverts the quasi-isomorphism of Step 5 by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], the complex $C_{E,L}$ is the scalar-extension representative when the regular K-flat complex $P=R_E[0]$ is used, as permitted by [lem-weil-constant-scalar-strict-unit]. Let $j_m:C_{E,L}\to T_m$ be the first cone projection followed by the $m$-th product projection. The normalization gives the strict identity $j_m\eta_{E,L}=u_m^{-1}\pi^L_m$. Composing its localized identity on the right with $Q(\eta_{E,L})^{-1}$ gives $Q(j_m)=Q(u_m^{-1}\pi^L_m)Q(\eta_{E,L})^{-1}$. This is the claimed compatibility of the inverse identification with every quotient projection; no uniqueness of an arbitrary isomorphism of homotopy limits is invoked.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2 and Lemma 6.8.2(1); the projection identity is the agent-written strict-coordinate refinement

proof.text: For the canonical self-reduction tower use the identity K-flat resolution of the regular complex, supplied by [lem-weil-constant-scalar-strict-unit]. Its reductionUnits isomorphisms and inverse tensor formulas identify the unit maps with the literal quotient projections and the transitions with coefficient reduction. Repeat the ordinary-limit and epimorphism arguments. The kernel short exact sequence of complexes supplies its distinguished triangle by Mathlib DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES_distinguished. The termwise product theorem and its projection-compatible product isomorphism transport this to a distinguished Roos triangle. Uniqueness of the legacy tower maps on pure tensors identifies this augmented tower with the one in [def-weil-derived-complete]. Choose a finite field of prime characteristic greater than l to witness the unrestricted predicate; this is auxiliary and imposes no condition on Y. Empty and disconnected Y, identity and ramified extensions are all allowed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NU-95e85b527 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no changes. This is the first split of an unsplit node (no repair note, no proof on the base) that Q21's PASSed re-split of lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible created. The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to side-live. The item is not in the drop list and is still unsplit in live. There are no new nodes. I read all eight steps against the cited statements. S1: the integers-DVR node plus clauses 2 and 3 of the valued-DVR node give finite, surjective A_{L,m}; the nonarchimedean hypothesis comes from clause 1 of def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, though the step does not say so (advisory). S2: sheafification is local (00WK) and the cokernel is the sheafified sectionwise cokernel, so local lifts make the reduction epi in Mod(R_L). S3: the strict-unit u_m, the sectionwise module limit and R_L as the sectionwise ring limit identify lim F_m with R_L as an R_L-module, with projections u_m^{-1}π_m. S4 and S6: clauses 1 and 2 of the surjective-tower node, which holds for any scheme and any commutative ring sheaf, give 1−s epi with kernel R_L, the derived product B and the Roos triangle. S5: the kernel-cocone node gives κ=(0,ι) as a quasi-isomorphism; the cone convention is sign-irrelevant because d_B=0; strict-unit uniqueness then gives κ=η exactly. S7: C_{E,L} is literally Rlim^c of def-weil-integral-scalar-extension with P=R_E[0]; the inverse projection identity is right composition. S8: with q=id, c_n=[γ_n]=u_n^{-1}π_n and t_n=[id⊗ρ_n] match the strict tower, so def-weil-derived-complete holds for E=L. Bhatt–Scholze Prop 3.1.10 (p.17) and Def 3.5.2 (p.24) checked; no SGA. Edge cases Y=∅, disconnected Y, ramified E⊂L and E=L checked, plus the small case Spec F_q with Q_ℓ. I accept the six declared tool_uses (arithmetic, sheafification, module limits, kernel-cocone). lem-fd-etale-integral-line-derived-complete overlaps only the E=L corollary (advisory).

lean.statement: theorem regular_scalar_unit_quasi_isomorphism (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{d}) (_hl : l ≠ D.p) (η : regularComplex l L Y ⟶ (integralScalarComplexFunctor l E L ι Y).obj (regularComplex l E Y)) (_hη : quotientCoordinates l E Y L ι η ∧ zeroSecondComponent l E Y L ι η) : (∀ n : ℕ, Finite (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l L (n + 1))) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (integralCoefficientSheafTransition l L Y n)) ∧ (∃ e : regularComplex l L Y ≅ limit (tower l E L ι Y), ∀ n : ℕ, e.hom ≫ limit.π (tower l E L ι Y) (op n) = leg l E L ι Y η n) ∧ QuasiIso η ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Fan.mk (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (product l E L ι Y)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.map (Pi.π (fun m : ℕ ↦ (tower l E L ι Y).obj (op m)) n)))) ∧ (∃ δ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (product l E L ι Y) ⟶ (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (regularComplex l L Y))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧, Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk (DerivedCategory.Q.map (inclusion l E L ι Y η)) (DerivedCategory.Q.map (boundary l E Y L ι)) δ ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l L Y))) ∧ (∃ e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((integralScalarComplexFunctor l E L ι Y).obj (regularComplex l E Y)) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (regularComplex l L Y), e.inv = DerivedCategory.Q.map η ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, e.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (leg l E L ι Y η n) = DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst (boundary l E Y L ι) ≫ Pi.π (fun m : ℕ ↦ (tower l E L ι Y).obj (op m)) n)) ∧ IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E Y none (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (regularComplex l E Y))
